description.p: img-fp finds copies of the same picture, even when they are not the same file. It compares images by their local features rather than by one hash of the whole picture, so it still finds a match after an image has been re-encoded, resized, cropped, rotated, recoloured, or placed inside a slide, collage or screenshot. Every match is checked against the pixels before it is shown.

ul.li: Exact copies under different names or in different folders
The same image saved again at a different size, quality or format
An image inside a larger one: a slide, a collage, a page, a screenshot

description.p: Pick folders and start the scan, then go through the groups and choose which images to move to the Trash. For each image the scan suggests whether to keep or delete it, never deleting the only copy of what a picture shows; nothing is marked until you ask. A copy can be compared with its group's reference, with the part each shows of the other outlined.
JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, AVIF, JPEG XL and more are read. The command-line tool is included as well: flatpak run --command=img-fp io.github.danielnara24.img-fp --help
